newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Koreans say no to pricey Mongolian dog meat.
newsitem.headline: Koreans say no to pricey Mongolian dog meat.

text.p: A South Korean company has turned its back on the chance to scoop up hundreds of kilograms of stray Mongolian dog meat because the price is too high, a dog-catching company in Ulan Bator said.
Mongolia's Noets Co, which shoots up to 60 stray dogs a day in Ulan Bator, had failed to clinch the dog meat export deal due to a disagreement over the price, the company said.
The South Korean importer had offered $0.20 per kg (2.2 lb) for the meat, to be transported frozen this winter, while Noets wanted $0.50 per kg, Noets manager Dayandorj told Reuters.
He declined to give the name of the South Korean company.
Noets Co sells stray dog skins to a local factory that makes them into fur coats and car seat covers, most of which are sold to Russian customers in Ulan Bator.
